key_insight: TEDDY is a compact pediatric foundation model that learns from ICD-coded diagnosis histories to forecast future disease risk and visit timing across many conditions.
clinical_relevance: It could help clinicians identify children at elevated risk earlier, including for rare diseases, using routinely collected EHR diagnostic trajectories rather than very large models or datasets.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Predicted first-occurrence disease onsets from prior diagnosis history and visit timing.
Compared against sex- and age-matched controls and multiple baselines, including DenseNet, CNN, RNN, LSTM, and a larger language model.
evidence_signal: Across 797 onset-prediction tasks in 16 ICD-10 chapters, TEDDY reached a median AUC of 72.0% and outperformed same-data baselines on 96-99% of tasks.
watch_item: The model was trained and evaluated at a single pediatric institution, so external validation and careful calibration are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
